title: Moments, levers and gears (physics only)

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Pivot
items.clue: The fixed point about which an object turns.

items.label: Moment of a force
items.clue: The turning effect of a push or pull about a fixed point.

items.label: Simple gear system
items.clue: Toothed wheels meshed together to pass on a rotational effect.

items.label: Lever
items.clue: A rigid bar that turns about a fixed point to pass on a turning effect.

questions.stem: A single steady force is applied to a gate that can swing freely on its hinges. In which case does the gate rotate?

options.text: When the line of action of the force does not pass through the hinges
Only when a second force acts on the gate at the same moment
Whenever the force is larger than the weight of the gate itself
Only when the force is applied exactly at the middle of the gate

questions.explanation: A force acting at some perpendicular distance from the pivot has a moment about it, so it turns the gate.

questions.stem: Which of these is an example of a force causing an object to rotate?

options.text: A crate pulled by a rope on each side, sliding straight along the floor
Pushing on the edge of a revolving door to make it turn
Two people pushing a stalled car forwards along a flat road
A ball falling straight downwards after being dropped

questions.explanation: The push acts at a distance from the central pivot, so it has a moment and the door rotates.

questions.stem: A force acts on a bar that can turn about a pivot. What is the turning effect of that force called?

options.text: The rotational force of the bar at the pivot
The leverage of the force acting on the bar
The moment of the force about the pivot
The work done by the force on the bar

questions.explanation: The specification states that the turning effect of a force is called the moment of the force.

questions.stem: The size of the moment of a force is defined by which equation?

options.text: moment of a force = weight × distance
moment of a force = force × length of bar
moment of a force = force divided by distance
moment of a force = force × distance

questions.explanation: This is the equation exactly as the specification gives it, written in symbols as M = F d.

questions.stem: Which row gives the units to use in the equation M = F d?

options.text: M in newton-metres, F in grams, d in metres
M in newton-metres, F in newtons, d in metres
M in newtons, F in newtons, d in metres
M in joules, F in newtons, d in metres

questions.explanation: These are the units the specification gives: Nm for the moment, N for the force and m for the distance.

questions.stem: A 2.0 kg bag hangs from a beam at a perpendicular distance of 0.30 m from the pivot. The gravitational field strength is 9.8 N/kg. What is the moment of the bag's weight about the pivot?

options.text: 5.9 Nm

questions.explanation: Weight = 2.0 x 9.8 = 19.6 N, so M = F d = 19.6 x 0.30 = 5.88 Nm, which is 5.9 Nm to two significant figures.

questions.stem: In the equation M = F d, what exactly is the distance d?

options.text: The distance measured along the object from the pivot to where it acts
The distance the object moves in the direction of the force as it turns
The distance from one end of the object across to its far end
The perpendicular distance from the pivot to its line of action

questions.explanation: This is the definition the specification gives, and it is measured in metres.

questions.stem: A 60 N push is applied to a door along a line of action that passes exactly through the hinge. Why does the door not turn?

options.text: The perpendicular distance from the hinge is zero
The push is too small to overcome the weight of the door
A single force can never make a heavy object rotate
The push is applied too high up on the face of the door

questions.explanation: With d = 0, M = F d gives a moment of zero however large the force is.

questions.stem: A force of 25 N acts at a perpendicular distance of 15 cm from a pivot. What is the moment of the force about the pivot?

options.text: 375 Nm

questions.explanation: 15 cm = 0.15 m, so M = F d = 25 x 0.15 = 3.75 Nm, with the distance in metres as the specification requires.

questions.stem: A gardener prises up a stone using a long-handled spade as a lever. Why is a long handle better than a short one?

options.text: The longer handle increases the size of the push the gardener makes
The lever gives out more energy than the gardener puts into it
A longer handle is heavier, so it presses on the stone harder
The same push acts at a greater distance, so its moment is larger

questions.explanation: M = F d, so increasing d while F stays the same increases the turning effect on the stone.

questions.stem: An object is balanced about a pivot. Which statement must be true?

options.text: The total clockwise moment equals the total anticlockwise moment
The total of the forces on one side equals the total on the other side
Each force must act the same distance from the pivot as the other one
The pivot must be exactly at the middle of the whole object

questions.explanation: This is the balanced condition exactly as the specification states it, about that same pivot.

questions.stem: A plank balances on a pivot. A 10 N weight sits 0.60 m to the left of the pivot, and a 30 N weight sits somewhere to the right. What can be said about the 30 N weight?

options.text: It sits further from the pivot, because a larger force turns more
It sits closer to the pivot, because its force is the larger
It sits the same distance out, as the plank is balanced
It cannot balance, since the two forces are not equal

questions.explanation: Equal moments with a larger force means a smaller distance: 0.20 m, one third of 0.60 m.
